The debugger reports the executable PE checksum cannot be verified (CheckSum 0) and ntdll symbols unavailable; neither message is interpreted as a matching-PDB failure.

levelmesh_vertices.interpretation: All nonnegative lindex values found in the complete vertex capacity are the zero-valued unused tail. The inspected prefix includes the one-element interior free span and all allocated CPU vertices.

material_metadata.limitation: These counts include unused allocator capacity. VkLevelMeshUploader::UploadUniforms resolves uTextureIndex in the CPU Uniforms element by reference before uploading it. The post-loss fields are still not a proof of bytes consumed by the failing submission, descriptor generations, material layer offsets or pipeline pairing.

source_contract.fact: Default null LevelMesh starts with one 1024 square atlas page.
CreateLightmap retires prior light/probe image objects and resizes Lightmaps to the new count.
The bindless binding is PARTIALLY_BOUND. UpdateBindlessDescriptorSet overwrites current page pairs; removed pairs are not rewritten.
Ordinary draw-list retirement follows the frame fence wait.
Negative aPosition.w emits vLightmapIndex=-1; nonnegative w resolves the reserved page pair.
Lightmap sampling is guarded by vLightmapIndex!=-1.
Lightmap probe gathering is guarded by vLightmapIndex!=-1 and no explicit environment probe.
UploadUniforms resolves material texture identity in the CPU Uniforms array element by reference before UploadData.

inferences: Ordinary CPU construction of live lightmap vertex indices is strongly negative for this exact run: no inspected allocated LevelMesh vertex or sector vertex selects a lightmap page.
The active CPU LevelMesh index extent cannot select the zero-index unused vertex tail.

The 1-to-0 page transition leaves the previous reserved descriptor pair referring to retired views. This is a source lifetime lead; because the binding is PARTIALLY_BOUND, unused invalid descriptors alone do not demonstrate a Vulkan violation or crash cause.

Remaining live alternatives include CPU-to-GPU upload/state mismatch or pipeline pairing, other dynamically selected resource paths, and application/driver interaction with the removed unused descriptor.
limitations: The process dump was captured after vkWaitForFences returned VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and renderer teardown; screen is null. It captures surviving CPU level/sector data, not application thread state before the GPU stall.
CPU arrays and active index extents do not prove the bytes consumed by the failing GPU submission, historical shader execution, exact descriptor generation or pipeline specialization.
The retired-image fault interval overlap is corroborating evidence, not unique causality or proof that the shader sampled that image.
The raw analysis is a new supplemental file. Historical STOP files, original run artifacts and their artifact index remain unchanged.
No production crash repair is claimed by this offline analysis.
